findings: Solved 2026-10-30 on the owner's request (exercises book by book, in Practice): Chapter 13 (Halogens) exercise as printed on PDF 302-304 (printed pages 302-304), in the book's words and order.

Counts: Q.1 ten MCQs (I-X); Q.2 sixteen short parts a-p, solved as 14 self-checks (b, the printed equation, joined with c, its question; n, a statement, joined with o, its question); Descriptive Q.3-Q.6 four questions. All solved in English and Roman Urdu.
No answer key is printed. MCQ keys worked out from the chapter: I d, II b, III b, IV c, V d, VI c, VII c, VIII c, IX b, X c.
Book correction, MCQ V: options lettered a), b), b), d); the third option (Br-) is option (c). Kept as printed in the stem; options given ids a-d with a Book correction box.
Book correction, Short b: equation printed unbalanced 'Br2 + 2I- -> Br- + I2'; correct Br2 + 2I- -> 2Br- + I2. Kept as printed with a Book correction box.
Book correction, Short p: refers to 'question l)' but the chlorine/NaOH equations are in part o). Kept as printed with a Book correction box.

Doubtful keys for the reviewer: MCQ IV says 'thermal stability of the halogens' (the chapter treats thermal stability of the hydrogen halides); keyed (c), true for both. MCQ VIII keyed (c) electronegativity per 13.4 (weak F-F bond, option b, is also a factor; noted in the explanation). MCQ IX keyed (b) 'partially soluble in dilute ammonia': the chapter says AgBr is sparingly soluble and dissolves in concentrated ammonia; (c) could be argued.
Answers use the chapter's corrected equations (unbalanced F2/X- displacement, 2HBr + H2SO4, 3Cl2 + 6NaOH with 5NaCl); Roman Urdu Wazahat boxes point this out.

Answers beyond the chapter, labelled: Short f (iodine/tincture of iodine as antiseptic and how it works; Chapter 16 lists tincture iodine for cuts), Short h (HF partial ionization equation), Short i (hydrogen bonding in HF), Short l (chlorinated by-products such as trihalomethanes), Q.3 (HI decomposing on a hot wire), Q.5 (3ClO- -> 2Cl- + ClO3-).
Comparison answers (Short j, Q.3, Q.5) carry answer tables. No figures. Draft for the academic review.
